name: Vim lite
author: Flow
description: A small set of Vim's keys for writing: Normal, Insert and Visual modes, motions, operators, counts, search, registers shared with the system clipboard, and macros. A widget beside undo and redo shows the mode and what each command just did.

settings.label: Start in
settings.description: The mode a script opens in.

settings.label: Leave Insert with
settings.description: Two keys typed quickly, such as jk, that work like Escape. Leave it empty to use only Escape.

settings.label: Also works as Escape
settings.description: A key that does what Escape does, such as Caps Lock. Click it, then press the key. With Caps Lock, letters still type as if it were off.

settings.label: Follow wrapped lines
settings.description: j, k and the up and down arrows move a row on screen, through lines that wrap. Off, they move a whole line of the script. With an operator, such as dj, they always take whole lines.

settings.label: Block cursor
settings.description: Outside Insert mode, draws the cursor over the character it's on.

settings.label: Cursor blinks
settings.description: Blinks the block cursor. In Insert mode the cursor is the system’s own, which blinks as the system is set to.
